clinical_observations.content: Sabrina participated in an in-clinic evaluation with her mother present. She demonstrated a generally cheerful and cooperative demeanor which facilitated initial engagement with the assessment tasks. Her muscle tone was observed to be within normal limits, with full active range of motion across major joints. However, Sabrina's attention span was noted to be short, with high levels of distractibility requiring repeated redirections and maximal visual and verbal cues. She was more successful in self-directed activities where she showed brief moments of focused engagement but struggled to maintain this in structured tasks. Fine motor coordination was challenged, particularly in tasks requiring bilateral integration and visual-motor precision, necessitating occasional hand-over-hand guidance. The necessity for frequent prompts and assistance did alter the administration and validity of standardized tests, warranting testing modifications to ensure best performance outcomes.
